title: Publish chain: push scenarios → JFRED → jfredToolsPlugin, verify clean-room + marketplace, sync wrapper clone
description:
Consolidated go-public checklist from four implementation-notes files:
(1) User must push the scenarios repo (1 unpushed commit 075ef56 "added S86, updated S41") BEFORE JFRED is pushed — JFRED's pin was fetched from the local clone and dangles for cloners until then.
(2) JFRED is staged but uncommitted; first commit + push still needs the privacy gate re-run at push time. Commit ordering: commit inside jfred/jfredToolsPlugin first, push, then re-stage the gitlink in JFRED (it currently records the license-only commit 70ad1b6), commit JFRED, then RevEng.
(3) Consider switching the GitHub default branch for matkatmusic/jfred from master (empty initial commit — a plain git clone gets an empty tool) to develop: `gh repo edit matkatmusic/jfred --default-branch develop`.
(4) After pushing jfredToolsPlugin to https://github.com/matkatmusic/jfredToolsPlugin, verify the install flow with a real `claude plugin marketplace add matkatmusic/jfredToolsPlugin` + `claude plugin install`, then decide whether the zshrc --plugin-dir wrapper (task 108's interim enablement) should be retired.
(5) ~/Programming/jfredToolsPlugin (the clone the claude() wrapper actually loads) does NOT yet have the two new scenario skills — pull/push the canonical $REVENG/jfred/jfredToolsPlugin changes into it after committing, or /impl-scenario and /plan-scenario won't resolve at the next launch (their RevEng copies are now archived).
(6) Deferred verifications left for the user from task 111: RevEng `npm test` (5 task-workflow tests + 2 python tests remain), `npm run typecheck`, clean-room `npm test`, and the interactive /run-scenario check under `command claude`.

title: Investigate: agent edit near JSONL line 77 has no timeline entry — pre-baseline trim drops the edit's event (baseline-demo)
description: In baseline-demo, the agent message at JSONL line 77 ('added least_valuable(store) ...') has no matching tool-result/edit entry in the timeline, so the JSONL line where the edit occurred can't be navigated to from the timeline. Confirmed mechanism candidate: when pre-baseline reconstruction is declined, seedBaseCommitBeacon (jfred/src/reconstruction_base_commit.ts:132) drops every FileEvent at-or-before the beacon insertion point ('dropped N superseded pre-baseline event(s)') — the edit's WriteEvent never survives, so no revision, no fileChanges chip, no timeline entry; the git-derived baseline synthetic turn (recordGitBaselineSnapshot, jfred/webapp/views/timeline-nodes.ts:69) absorbs only the gitBase snapshot, it does not literally merge the edit. Verify against the baseline-demo session (was preBaseline declined? does the entry appear when accepted?), then decide the fix: even when trimmed, the turn should probably still be navigable to its JSONL line even if its file event is superseded.

title: Timeline: red '(abandoned)' pill on the last row of each abandoned branch
description: The last timeline row of an abandoned (rewound) branch needs an '(abandoned)' pill-tag, colored red — the dimming alone doesn't announce where a dead branch ENDS. Data already present: every node copies the engine's per-record branch-membership stamp isOrphaned (jfred/webapp/views/timeline-types.ts:33; tool rows carry it too, :230) — the pill goes on each orphaned RUN's tip: a node with isOrphaned true whose next node in context.nodes is not orphaned (or that is the final node). Render site: the row badge spot in timeline-render-rows.ts where the FAILED badge is appended (`el('span', { class: 'failed-badge', text: 'FAILED' })`) — same pattern, new class (e.g. .abandoned-badge, red) in webapp/styles.css. Watch interleaved multi-session timelines: 'next node' should mean next node of the SAME session (node.sessionId) so a branch tip isn't masked by another session's surviving row landing after it.

title: Paths... popover -> settings WIZARD: design the flow (mockup first), then implement
description:
DIRECTION CHANGE 2026-07-21 (supersedes the earlier two-section-popover mockup): the Paths... popover should become a settings WIZARD:
- screen 1: set the project path
- screen 2: 'do you wish to set a custom file history snapshot path or auto-derive the path?'
- screen 3: 'do you wish to set a Git Repo path?'
- screen 4: 'do you wish to pick a git repo commit? (default: master branch tip)'
DELIVERABLE ORDER: (a) define the wizard's flow logic via UI/UX MOCKUP first, (b) define how values are CHANGED for a session after it loads (re-enter the wizard? jump to a single screen? a compact summary panel with per-row edit?), (c) only then implement. The user says ambiguities must be flushed out first — resolve these in the mockup step:
(1) TRIGGER: when does the wizard run — first launch with no config? every folder switch? on demand from the Paths... button? (screen 1 is GLOBAL config, screens 2-4 are effectively per-project — reveng-paths.json entries — so does the wizard rerun per project?)
(2) Screen-2 default: auto-derive (today's behavior — empty posts '' and the server re-derives, app-header.ts computeFileHistoryDirToPost).
(3) Screen-4 default 'master branch tip': which ref when the repo's default branch isn't master, and should the default instead be the commit the SESSION records (the s85-style recorded baseline) when one exists?
(4) Skip semantics: declining screens 3/4 must leave the project reconstructing exactly as with no reveng-paths entry.
(5) Persistence: where each screen's answer lands (screen 1 -> /api/config global; screens 2-4 -> /api/project-paths, persist flag) and whether the wizard's finish step is the 137-style 'store?' prompt.
(6) The task-56 pre-baseline question ('reconstruct file states preceding the baseline commit?') fires at project load — decide whether it becomes a wizard screen or stays a load-time dialog.
CARRY-OVERS still wanted from the pre-wizard design: picker-button naming 'Set Projects Folder location' / 'Set Git Repo location'; Store subsumes Apply (postProjectPaths(true) applies AND persists, app-paths-project.ts:122-123); commit pick list = task 154's 500-newest list (search box open there). Existing code sites: #paths-popover jfred/webapp/index.html:17-40, app-header.ts, app-paths-project.ts, /api/project-paths route.

title: Represent script moves as true rename revisions (merge source history into destination)
description:
Residue from tasks 142-145: the moved-away SOURCE files (`one.py`, `two.py`, `three.py` in s85) still show as alive 1-revision histories in the Files nav — the engine's script channels record no delete/rename revision for them, so the tree shows both `one.py` and `core_one.py` (the latter now badged '← one.py'). Representing script moves as true rename revisions (merging source history into the destination via reconstruction_lineage) is the real fix and needs its own planned change against the full 87-scenario sweep.
Also verify while sweeping: the trunk absorb also un-orphans the absorbed records in every OTHER parallel-tool-call transcript (any newer-CC capture), which may shift timelines that previously dimmed those rows as rewound. The scenario suite will say; nothing in the 21 branch tests regressed.

description:

Implementation findings (scouted, no code changed):

title: Raw Lines rows: color the line classification distinctly, drop 'Invalid Date', show the { } inspector button
description:
Three fixes for the task-134 Raw Lines rows (kind jsonl-line), scouted 2026-07-21:
1) CLASSIFICATION COLOR: the row text is one string `${verdict.type} · ${verdict.verdict}` (webapp/views/timeline-line-nodes.ts:71) rendered in a single .tl-text span whose class comes from computeRoleClass(kind) — LINE_NODE_KIND falls through to 'role-end' (timeline-render-row-cells.ts:38), so the classification renders in the same color as message text. Split the type/verdict into its own span (or a role pill — computeRolePillLabel in timeline-labels.ts:193 currently returns undefined for line nodes) with a distinct CSS class.
2) INVALID DATE: LineNode.when = verdict.timestamp ?? '' (timeline-line-nodes.ts:68) and the row renderer always prints new Date(node.when).toLocaleString() (timeline-render-rows.ts:110) — empty when → 'Invalid Date'. Two-sided fix: the engine's LineVerdict (src/reconstruction_line_verdicts.ts) should populate timestamp whenever the raw record carries a date field; the renderer should print '' (not Invalid Date) when when is empty/unparseable.
3) MISSING { } BUTTON: checkRowCarriesJsonRecordButton (timeline-sessions.ts:118) returns false when node.uuid === undefined, which covers most raw-line-only records (summary lines etc.), so their JSON can't be inspected. The verdict already knows its 0-based line number (WireLineVerdict.line) but deriveLineNodes drops it — carry `line` onto LineNode, always show { } on jsonl-line rows, and open the inspector by line number instead of uuid.
